name: Engine structure and a renderer to learn from
body:
Dean (2026-11-07): "before [building another renderer] can i get the lantern's engine refactored so that it's ready to help me with that. I'd like for the renderer to be well documented and abstracted so that i can easily follow along with the implementation that is there and recreate it in [another] engine. i think having a clean application and game-loop would also be really helpful." He pointed at the engine in the snake repository (branch game-with-engine-architecture) as the structure to follow: a domain per folder, interfaces with their domain, one facade folder per third-party library split by domain, an Application with a clear life cycle and a game loop with fixed steps.

Target layout and what moved: docs/engine-structure.md. Behaviour must not change: every test passes, and the game, the stub and the editor run as before.

Decisions (provisional, 2026-11-07, not yet reviewed by Dean):
- Snake's folder pattern, but no dependency-injection container: the Application creates each object and passes it on, as Lantern did before.
- File names stay PascalCase.nox (Lantern's Nox convention) rather than snake's kebab-case; folders follow snake.
- The application lives in its own top-level folder, not engine/application: tests build engine/ without the GPU, the host or SDL, and the application needs all of them.
- Namespaces keep their names where only the folder moved (lantern:::sdl, lantern:::gpu, lantern:::engine), so the change stays a move; only RenderBackend, RenderReport, HeadlessRenderer and Frustum change namespace, to lantern:::renderer.

comments.text: Built on branch claude/project-thread-v1k4t4: 189/189 tests, check-window passes, stub, platformer and editor run on Linux (Xvfb, lavapipe). Not yet run on macOS. Waiting on review and Dean's merge.
